sources.primary_title: Pakistan tech firms eye deeper Saudi foothold as they head to Riyadh for LEAP 2026
sources.verified_angle_summary: Pakistani technology companies are leveraging LEAP 2026 to expand their footprint in Saudi Arabia's rapidly growing digital economy. The delegation, supported by the Pakistan Software Export Board and Trade Development Authority of Pakistan, features a dedicated pavilion with 20 companies. Pakistan's IT Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja is attending to inaugurate the pavilion and deliver a keynote. Returning firms like ByteCorp and KAACIB are building on previous successes, with KAACIB opening a Riyadh office. Newer entrants are tailoring products for Saudi real estate, logistics, and enterprise technology, such as Stellisys offering ZATCA-compliant invoicing. This specific angle highlights cross-border tech expansion and the tangible business impact of LEAP 2026, distinct from general event overviews.
sources.verified_key_facts: Pakistan has a dedicated pavilion at LEAP 2026 featuring 20 technology companies; The pavilion is supported by the Pakistan Software Export Board and Trade Development Authority of Pakistan; Pakistan's IT Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja is attending LEAP 2026 to inaugurate the pavilion and deliver a keynote; KAACIB is opening a local office in Riyadh following its participation in LEAP 2025; Stellisys is showcasing a Saudi version of its platform with ZATCA-compliant invoicing and an AI layer; Pakistan's participation in LEAP 2025 generated $9.74 million in business and 78 leads according to PSEB.
